findings.title: Foot sampler's clear() test has no float tolerance, so the sampler rejects the exact-fit multi-wire foot; k=3 under measured rules is feasible but practically never found
findings.detail: In `_draw_feet`, `clear(a0)` checks `abs(...) >= ps` with no epsilon. Take k=3 wires at pitch 0.625 mm with the signal feet spread to +-0.25 mm (the sampler's own spread value). The only legal first foot is one `ps` from the gate wire, and the distance comes out as 0.6249999999999991 mm, below 0.625 mm, for every die u0 I tried. The 'clear' branch (taken with probability 0.6) therefore never accepts it; it can only be hit by chance in the unconstrained branch. Effect under `case4_measured_spec`: over 15000 raw draws the generator accepts 198 layouts at k=1 but only 1 at k=3, and `generate(k=3, 20, max_failures=5000)` raises RuntimeError. Yet the reference topology with 3 wires per die and sampler-reachable feet passes `check` with 0 violations. The claimed default-rule k=2/3 results are not affected. The defect limits the claim of 'searchable wire feet' in tight cases. It also shows that a RuntimeError from the generator is not evidence of infeasibility.
findings.evidence: Scratch run: clear() distance 0.6249999999999991 for u0 = 28, 22.5, 31, 17.5. Accepted per 15000 draws: k=1 198, k=3 1. A hand-built Params (case4_reference_params, LS feet 29.375/30/30.625, sigfeet LS (-0.25, 0, 0.25, 0)) on the measured spec with k=3 gives check() == [].
findings.suggested_check: Compare with a tolerance (`>= ps - 1e-9`), then re-measure k=3 acceptance under measured rules.

findings.title: 'Exactly 2 feasible' under measured rules rests on the generator's own sampler for orientation y
findings.detail: Orientation 0 is excluded by a closed form of necessary conditions, and the feasible pair is witnessed by DRC-clean layouts. I re-ran seeds 6 and 9 and got the same two sequences. Orientation y, however, is excluded only by 12000 draws of `_sample` plus `_quick_ok`, which is the same sampler that, per the finding above, misses feasible regions. The docstring admits 'sampled, not a closed form' but still asserts 'exactly 2 are feasible'.
findings.evidence: test_case4_orientation_y_has_no_candidate_under_measured_rules uses D._sample, so it tests the sampler's prior, not the parameter space.
findings.suggested_check: Word it as 'none found by the sampler for orientation y' or add a closed-form bound.

findings.title: The closed-form 2 mm pitch infeasibility proof covers only LS dies that sit over the signal strips' x-range
findings.detail: The bound (Kelvin_max - gate_min)/2 = 1.35 mm assumes the LS gate and Kelvin wires run straight down across the source pad. That holds only if the die's signal feet lie within the LS strips' x-range of 25.3..64.7 mm. For a die outside that range the wires run diagonally, and a hand computation gives a power-foot distance of about 3.3 mm for a die at x = 15 mm. Such placements are probably excluded by other constraints (the DC- pad, the 25 mm Kelvin limit), but the test does not show this. The generator's RuntimeError is sampling evidence only; with 20000 draws I still found no candidate.
findings.evidence: Keepouts: KELVIN_LS [25,10,65,18], GATE_LS [25,20,65,28]. Pads: gate x [-1.5,-0.5], kelvin [0.5,1.5], source [-1.665,1.835]. generate(2 mm rules, k=1, max_failures=20000) raised RuntimeError.
findings.suggested_check: Extend the closed form to dies outside the strips' x-range, or state the assumption.

findings.title: The throughput paragraph in the docstring was not re-measured after the sampler change
findings.detail: The unchanged docstring still states 244-253 DRC-valid candidates/s on Case 4 with k=1. With this commit I measured 53.5/s and 48.1/s, while two other test processes were running. The measurement is inconclusive, but the claim is now unverified.
findings.evidence: Scratch timing of D.generate(case4_spec(), 300, seed=1 and seed=2).
findings.suggested_check: Re-run the documented timing on an idle machine and update the paragraph.

caveats: The multi-wire result is demonstrated under default rules only. Under the measured rules, k=3 is feasible but the sampler almost never finds it (float-tolerance defect in clear()).
The 'exactly 2 feasible topologies under measured rules' statement is proven by a closed form only for orientation x. Orientation y is excluded by sampling only.
The 2 mm pitch infeasibility proof assumes vertical signal wires, i.e. LS dies over the signal strips.
Case 4 gate/Kelvin pads and the 25 mm signal-wire limit are assumptions, so all Case 4 limits hold only under those assumptions.
